questions.stem: At which Indian National Congress session was 'Vande Mataram' publicly sung for the very first time as a Congress anthem?

options.option_text: 1885 Bombay session, the inaugural INC meeting under W.C. Bonnerjee
1896 Calcutta session, where Rabindranath Tagore performed the song on stage
1906 Calcutta session, presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji as Congress President
1911 Delhi Durbar session, the first Congress meet held in the capital city

questions.explanation: B is correct: 'Vande Mataram' from Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's novel Anandamath was first sung at the 1896 Calcutta Congress session by Rabindranath Tagore. Option A is wrong as the 1885 founding session predates the song's political use by over a decade; Option C is a common confusion because the 1906 Calcutta session was famous for the Surat Split foreshadowing, not this song.

questions.stem: The Rowlatt Act (1919), which allowed detention without trial and triggered Gandhi's first nationwide satyagraha, was officially known by which name?

options.option_text: The Seditious Meetings Prevention Act, banning large political gatherings
The Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act, enabling indefinite preventive detention
The Indian Press Emergency Powers Act, restricting nationalist publications
The Public Safety Ordinance, empowering arrests without any judicial sanction

questions.explanation: B is correct: The Rowlatt Act's official title was the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act, 1919, extending wartime emergency powers into peacetime and allowing magistrates to detain suspects without trial or charge. Option A (Seditious Meetings Act) was a separate 1907 colonial law targeting public assemblies, often confused with the Rowlatt Act.

questions.stem: Under the 'tinkathia' system in Champaran that Gandhi challenged through his 1917 satyagraha, indigo cultivators were compelled to do which of the following?

options.option_text: Pay rent at three times the prevailing rate directly to British indigo planters
Cultivate indigo on 3 out of every 20 kathas of their entire leased landholding
Supply three months of unpaid labour every year inside indigo processing factories
Surrender one-third of their total annual crop output to European zamindars directly

questions.explanation: B is correct: 'Tinkathia' derives from 'teen katha' — cultivators had to grow indigo on 3 out of every 20 kathas (15%) of their holding as compulsory rent-in-kind for European planters. Option C confuses this with 'begar' (forced unpaid labour), a different but contemporaneous form of exploitation Gandhi also addressed in Champaran.

questions.stem: Which major provision of the Government of India Act 1935, though duly enacted by Parliament, was never actually brought into operative force before Indian independence?

options.option_text: Provincial autonomy in eleven provinces, which the Congress rejected outright in 1937
The All-India Federation, as too few princely states formally acceded to trigger it
Bicameral legislatures in all provinces, strongly opposed by Muslim League councils
Separate communal electorates for Scheduled Castes, reversed later by the Poona Pact

questions.explanation: B is correct: The federal provisions required at least half the princely states by population to accede — they refused, so the All-India Federation was never constituted. Option A is wrong: provincial autonomy was indeed implemented from April 1937 when Congress formed governments in seven provinces, making it the only part of the 1935 Act that came into force.

questions.stem: The Ghadar Party, founded in 1913 among Indian immigrants in North America, published its revolutionary organ 'Ghadar' newspaper from which city?

options.option_text: London, where Shyamji Krishna Varma had already established the India House network
San Francisco, operating from the 'Yugantar Ashram' as the party headquarters
Toronto, then the largest hub of Punjabi Sikh diaspora in early twentieth-century Canada
Berlin, where the Indian Independence Committee also operated throughout World War I

questions.explanation: B is correct: The Ghadar Party's headquarters was the 'Yugantar Ashram' in San Francisco, from where Lala Har Dayal and colleagues published the multilingual 'Ghadar' paper in Urdu, Punjabi, Gujarati and other languages. Option D is a common distractor — the Berlin Indian Independence Committee was a separate World War I-era body with overlapping goals but no organisational link to the Ghadar Party.

questions.stem: At the Lucknow Pact of 1916, the Indian National Congress accepted separate Muslim electorates. What did the Muslim League formally agree to in exchange for this Congress concession?

options.option_text: Joint Hindu-Muslim civil disobedience campaigns against the British administration
The Congress demand for responsible self-government and constitutional reforms in India
A guaranteed one-third Muslim reservation in every central legislative committee seat
Recognition of Hindi as the sole language of all inter-provincial administration

questions.explanation: B is correct: The Lucknow Pact was a bargain — Congress conceded separate electorates and agreed to weightage for Muslims in minority provinces; the League backed the Congress demand for self-government and constitutional reforms from Britain. Option C is wrong because it conflates the pact's electoral weightage clauses with a separate reservation system that was never part of the 1916 agreement.

questions.stem: The Hindustan Republican Association's 1924 manifesto titled 'The Revolutionary', authored by Sachindra Nath Sanyal, envisioned replacing British rule with which specific form of government for India?

options.option_text: A parliamentary democracy modelled on universal adult franchise and guaranteed civil rights
A federal republic called the 'United States of India' with equal rights for all citizens
A socialist workers' state with collective ownership of all major industrial production
A constitutional monarchy retaining Indian princes as legitimate ceremonial figureheads

questions.explanation: B is correct: The HRA's 1924 manifesto explicitly called for a 'Federal Republic of the United States of India', drawing on the American federal model and demanding equal rights regardless of caste or creed. Option C is the most tempting distractor — socialist ideology was only formally adopted later when the HRA was reconstituted as the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) in 1928 under Bhagat Singh's ideological influence.
